newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thanksgiving, profit-taking knock Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Thanksgiving, profit-taking knock Singapore shares.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) of shares closed down on Thursday as a day of blue chip profit-taking in Singapore coincided with the Thanksgiving holiday on Wall Street.
The STII fell just below the psychologically important 2,200 level to close down 20.69 points at 2,199.67.
But most dealers were confident of buyers returning to the market next week to get the index back safely above 2,200.
"There is underlying firmness, so I don't think there's any real concern about the fall," said one local dealer. Volume was a modest 134.23 million shares, with 99 gainers and 250 losers.
Fraser & Neave was the STII's biggest casualty, down Singapore $0.40 at S$14.90 on 338,000 shares traded.
Earlier firmness on Singapore's over-the-counter UOB-OTC index was also eroded by the close. It ended the day down 3.88 points at 1,223.70.
Shares in Malaysian companies were the best performers.
Samanda Holdings was the biggest gain, up S$0.35 at S$7.50, while compatriot auto firm, Tan Chong Motor, was the most active share, with 20.44 million units traded.
